messages.content: start Docker on window using docker start.

function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a given command using the os.system() function specifically for Windows operating systems. For multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For complex tasks, create and run a .bat file. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The Windows command line instruction(s) to be executed. Use '&&' between commands for multiple instructions. For complex sequences, encapsulate the logic within a .bat file and provide the execution command here.

message.reasoning:
The user says "start Docker on window using docker start." They want to start Docker on Windows using docker start. But docker start is used to start containers, not the Docker daemon. To start Docker service, you need to start the Docker Desktop or the Docker Engine service. On Windows, you can use `net start com.docker.service` or `Start-Service -Name com.docker.service`. Or if using Docker Desktop, you can launch the application. The user might want to start Docker engine via command line. So we can provide a command: `net start com.docker.service`. Or using PowerShell: `Start-Service -Name com.docker.service`. Or if using Docker Desktop, you can open it from Start menu.

We should respond with a command. The tool expects a Windows command line instruction. So we can give: `net start com.docker.service`. That will start the Docker service. Alternatively, if they want to start Docker Desktop, we can instruct to run `& "C:\Program Files\Docker\Docker\Docker Desktop.exe"`. But the simplest is `net start com.docker.service`.

Thus we call the function with command: `net start com.docker.service`.
